# <span id="aanchor205"></span> Tank Editor - Tools

[&lt;&lt; Back to Tank Editor](Tank%20Editor.md#Menu)

The following options are available on the Tank Editor Tools menu:

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Contact Selections">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Contact Selections</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Contact Selections">

Users can assign contacts to tanks, similarly to meters, locations, and quality sources. Assigning contacts to tanks allows for notifications based on messages and exceptions. Typically, these will be generated when importing TFX files with gauge tickets and tank run tickets.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Validations">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Ticket Validations</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Validations">

<span id="TicketVal"></span>This option allows users to attach validation templates to a tank to validate attached tickets. See [Ticket Validations](../Locations/Location%20Editor/Tools%20-%20Ticket%20Validations.md) for additional information.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Info">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Info</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Info">

The Info screen contains the following items:

- **Fluid Phase** - The fluid phase of a tank is always "Liquid".

- **Requires Close Approval** - Tanks that require close approval have to satisfy a set of conditions before they can be closed, and are closed manually in Location Close Approval.

- **Weekly Schedule** - This drop-down will list schedules created using the [Annual Schedule Editor](../Settings%20Manager/Application/Annual%20Schedule%20Editor.md). Location rollups will calculate totals for the tank according to the date spans defined by the schedule selected here.

  **Tip:** Checking the Calculate Weekly Totals option in System Configuration will make the Weekly Schedule option visible for the locations, tanks, and caverns in that system.

- **Ticket Import** - Ticket import options are used to enable adjustment of ticket dates for daylight savings time or for time zone. When these options are enabled, dates on all tickets that are imported into the location via TFX or FLOWCAL text file format are adjusted. (See: [Date and Time Adjustments During Import](../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Date%20and%20Time%20Adjustments%20During%20Import.md))
  - **Time Zone Shift** - When enabled, all dates and times are adjusted by the offset amount defined for the selected time zone. (Time zones are created using the [Time Zone Editor](../Settings%20Manager/Geographic/Time%20Zone%20Editor.md).) For these purposes the time zone offset is to be user-configured based on the offset from the company's standard business time zone rather than offsets from UTC.
  - **DST Shift** - When enabled, all dates and times occurring during daylight saving time are shifted forward one hour. All dates and times that occur outside of daylight saving time are imported.
  - **Time Zone** - This read-only field displays the current time zone of the location.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Product Conversion">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Product Conversion</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Product Conversion">

Product conversion tickets can be entered if the contents of a tank need to be converted from one product to another. When entering a Product Conversion ticket, only products that have been set up in the Product Editor with a product to be converted to can be converted. Only products that have a non-zero inventory in the tank at the effective date of the conversion ticket can be selected.

<div class="procedure">

To generate a product conversion ticket:

Go to **Tools** \> **Product Conversion** in the Tank Editor.

When creating a ticket from this screen, the location field will be locked to the selected tank.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 208;height: 196;" />

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Tank Empty">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Tank Empty</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Tank Empty">

If a tank is empty, but due to measurement inaccuracies, FLOWCAL does not have the tank inventory at zero, an Inventory Empty ticket can be created. When this is done, a ticket will be assigned to the tank that backs out any volume in the tank. If the calculated volume in the tank is negative, then the direction of the ticket will be adjusted to account for this.

<div class="procedure">

To generate an inventory empty ticket:

Go to **Tools** \> **Tank Empty** in the Tank Editor. The Inventory Empty screen will display, requesting date information and advanced empty settings. After initializing and confirming the empty, an inventory empty ticket will be generated and the tank's inventory level will be zeroed out at the specified time.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 336;height: 144;" />

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Capacity Table">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Capacity Table</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Capacity Table">

A capacity table (strapping table, calibration table) is generated by the company that performs the field determination of how much volume a tank holds at specified tank levels. A capacity table in FLOWCAL consists of datetime effective settings for tank dimensions and calculation specifics, such as level resolution and floating roof weight, and the volume/level information.

FLOWCAL capacity tables are identified by name and a tank may have more than one capacity table. Each named capacity table is a distinct set of the date effective data described above. Some example reasons for having multiple capacity tables on a tank include separate tables for high leg and low leg roof configurations, and alternate tables that depend on product density.

Once the tank has been created, one or more named capacity tables can be added using the Capacity Table editor or the Capacity Table import.

##### Capacity Table Editor

If the tank does not already have a capacity table, the capacity table editor will open in “New Table” mode; otherwise, the user will be able to edit an existing capacity table or create a new one.

The **New** button in the Capacity Table Editor includes a drop-down menu with the following options:

- **Table** - Creates a new named table. This operation is used to create an alternate capacity table with its own set of setup and volume/level information.
- **Data** - Data creates new set of date effective data for the currently selected named table. This operation is used to add new tank calibration data or to alter the table setup information.

<div class="procedure">

To create a new named capacity table:

1.  Launch the Tank Editor and go to **Tools** \> **Capacity Table**.
2.  Select **Table** from the **New** button drop-down.

To create a new data effective data set on an existing named capacity table:

1.  Launch the Tank Editor and go to **Tools** \> **Capacity Table**.
2.  Select the desired capacity table (field 1).
3.  Select **Data** from the **New** button drop-down.

To edit an existing date effective data set:

1.  Launch the Tank Editor and go to **Tools** \> **Capacity Table**.
2.  Select the desired capacity table (field 1).
3.  Select the desired effective date (field 2).



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 584;height: 417;" />

</div>

##### Capacity Table Setup Tab

<div class="procedure">

1.  If in new mode, set the start and end dates.

2.  Set the reference temperature. The units are based on the temperature units for the tank set in [Tank Units &amp; Options](Configuration/Tank%20Editor_Config%20-%20Units-Options%20Tab.md).

3.  Indicate if a shell temperature correction (CTSh) needs to be applied.

4.  Indicate if the CTSh is built into the capacity table.

5.  If the tank has a floating roof (upright cylindrical tanks only):
    1.  Enter a value for the leg height at the time of calibration. An exception will be written when the innage or outage level is below leg height.

    2.  Enter the data for the floating roof adjustment (FRA). Different options are available depending on whether the FRA Built Into Table option is enabled.

        FRA/FRC will not apply to the tank volume if the product level is below the configured tank leg height.

6.  If Enable Vapor Space Calculations is selected, the vapor space will be evaluated for corresponding tickets, and entering values into dead space will account for the dead space of the tank when evaluating the total vapor present in the tank.

    The required fields in the Capacity Table editor are highlighted in green. You will not be allowed to save until all required fields are populated. These fields will vary based on tank type.

7.  Select whether the capacity table to be entered is Innage or Outage. Innage measurement is relative to the bottom of the tank. Outage (aka Ullage) measurement is relative to a level at the top of the tank.

8.  Select how the data for the capacity table will be entered.

    If the capacity table to be entered has the tank volume at each level, select Volume and Level. If the capacity table to be entered has the volume for each increment in each section along with the number of increments in the section, select Increments per Zone/Volume per Increment. If the user chooses Increments per Zone/Volume per Increment, FLOWCAL will calculate the volume at each level when the capacity table is saved. The user can also switch between Table Entry Type options while entering the capacity table, but FLOWCAL will set the increments per zone to one and recalculate the volume per zone when the option Volume and Level is selected.

9.  Select **Table Resolution Entry**. This impacts data entry on the capacity table Data tab and entry of open, close, and gauge levels on tickets. Options vary based on the level units set on the tank:
    - **Feet** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet
    - **Inches** - Enter capacity table values as whole inches
    - **1/2 inch** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet, whole inches and 0–1<sup>1</sup>/<sub>2</sub> inches
    - **1/4 inch** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet, whole inches and 0–3<sup>1</sup>/<sub>4</sub> inches
    - **1/8 inch** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet, whole inches and 0–7<sup>1</sup>/<sub>8</sub> inches
    - **1/16 inch** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet, whole inches and 0–15<sup>1</sup>/<sub>16</sub> inches
    - **1/32 inch** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet, whole inches and 0–31<sup>1</sup>/<sub>32</sub> inches
    - **0.1 Foot** - Enter capacity table values as tenths of a foot; ex.: 10.1
    - **0.01 Foot** - Enter capacity table values as hundredths of a foot; ex.: 10.13

10. Click the **Save** button.

</div>

##### Capacity Table Data Tab

<div class="procedure">

To add capacity table data:

1.  Right-click on an existing row and choose **Insert Row Above** or **Insert Row Below**. A row will be added.
2.  Enter data for each cell.
3.  Click **Save**.
4.  To delete a row from the grid, right-click on an existing row and choose **Delete Row**. The highlighted row will be removed.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 508;height: 263;" />

</div>

</div>
